title: Nobody came to my Friendsgiving
author: Storytime
hook: I cooked Friendsgiving for twelve people. Nobody showed up. Then I found out where they all were.
story: So every year I host Friendsgiving. It's my favorite day of the year. This year I sent the invites in September. Twelve people said yes. I spent three hundred dollars on food and two days cooking. My ex, Ryan, used to help me plan it, and after we broke up he asked me for my recipes. For his mom, he said. Weird, but fine. On the day, I set the table. Six o'clock. Nobody. Seven o'clock. Nobody. I texted the group chat. No replies. At eight, my cousin finally texted me a screenshot. It was an invite. Friendsgiving, hosted by Ryan. Same date. Same time. Same menu. My menu. Word for word. Even my cranberry brie bites, the ones I invented. He had sent it to all my friends a week after mine, and told them I had canceled because I was too sad after the breakup. Half of them sent him money for the food. Then my cousin sent one more photo. Ryan, standing in front of my friends, giving a toast. Holding a plate of my brie bites. So I put my food in containers, got in my car, and drove to his place. Part two if you want to know what happened at the door.
caption: he stole my friends AND my recipes 🦃 #storytime
sound: a tense, slow-building cinematic sound at very low volume
why: Friendsgiving no-show stories regularly go viral before Thanksgiving, the recipe request is a planted clue that pays off, and the drive to his place is a strong part two cliffhanger.

title: Boyfriend split every bill to the cent
author: Storytime
hook: My boyfriend split every single bill with me, down to the cent. Then I found his spreadsheet.
story: My boyfriend Sam and I have been together for three years. And for three years, everything has been fifty fifty. Rent. Groceries. If he paid four dollars and twelve cents for coffee, I'd get a request for two dollars and six cents. Last Sunday, he left his laptop open, and I saw a spreadsheet called Sarah. That's me. I thought, here it is. Every cent I've ever owed him. I opened it. The first tab was exactly that. Every bill, every coffee, every split. But there was a second tab. It was called Matching. Every time I paid him back, he put the same amount into a savings account. Forty dollars for groceries. Six hundred for rent. For three years. The total at the bottom said eleven thousand four hundred dollars. And next to it, a link to a jewelry store. A ring. In my size. The problem is, the night before, I had told my sister I was thinking about breaking up with him. Because of the money thing. And my sister has never kept a secret in her life. Part two?
caption: the fifty fifty was for a reason 💍 #storytime
sound: a soft, romantic piano with a slight tension at very low volume
why: Splitting bills 50/50 is a hot debate topic, the absurdly exact cents set up the reveal, and the sister detail turns a sweet twist into a cliffhanger.

title: Neighbor parked in my driveway
author: Storytime
hook: My neighbor parked in my driveway for six months and said it was technically his. So I paid for a land survey.
story: When I bought my house last spring, the neighbor, Greg, came over with a beer and a smile. Then he parked his truck in my driveway. Every single day. When I asked him to move it, he laughed and said, technically, half of this driveway is mine. The old owner never minded. I asked to see proof. He said everyone on the street knows. For six months I parked on the road while he parked in my driveway. In the snow. So I finally paid eight hundred dollars for a professional land survey. Greg watched the surveyors the whole day, arms crossed, smiling. Then they put the little orange flags in the ground. The driveway was mine. All of it. But that wasn't the surprising part. The flags kept going. Past the driveway. Across his lawn. And they stopped right in the middle of his garage. Three feet of Greg's garage is on my property. Turns out, the old owner didn't mind his truck, because the old owner was his brother in law. Greg hasn't parked in my driveway since. But now he wants me to sign a paper saying the garage line doesn't matter. What would you do?
caption: the orange flags did NOT stop at the driveway 🚩 #storytime
sound: a confident, groovy bass line at very low volume
why: Entitled neighbor plus a satisfying reversal, the word technically is set up early and backfires, and the final question gets people arguing in the comments.
